description.en-US: The fulfillment this attempt tried to deliver. Immutable: an attempt is a record of one physical event against one delivery, and repointing it would move the evidence of what a machine did to a sale it never touched.

Which try this was, counting from 1. Unique per fulfillment, which is what makes the max_attempts policy countable and stops two concurrent requests both claiming to be attempt 2. Assigned under the per-order lock rather than by a sequence, because it counts tries at ONE delivery and a global counter would say nothing useful.

Snapshot of which sales point was asked to hand the goods over. Recorded per attempt rather than read from the fulfillment because the target may move between tries: an attempt is evidence about a specific machine, and after a reassignment the fulfillment no longer names the one that failed.

How this try ended, derived from its items rather than asserted: all dispensed is succeeded, none is failed, some is partially_succeeded. It stays pending until a result arrives, and a pending attempt is what blocks a second one — two machines acting on one reservation would hand over goods that were paid for once. Moved only by the attempt services, which is what no_update expresses.

The token handed to the executor and echoed back in its result, so a reply can be matched to the try that caused it. Distinct from result_event_id: this identifies the REQUEST and is generated here, while the event id identifies the REPLY and is generated by whoever reports it. A device that only knows an order code carries this in the command payload.

The reporter's own id for the result event, null until one arrives. Unique per organization, which is the whole idempotency mechanism: a duplicate delivery of the same event finds the stored attempt and replays its answer instead of dispensing the goods twice. Nullable and therefore a partial unique, because every attempt is created without one.

A digest of the result payload that was applied. Stored so a redelivery can be told apart from a CONTRADICTION: the same event id with the same payload is a replay and is answered from the record, while the same id with a different payload means two different claims about one physical event, which is refused rather than guessed at.

What Inventory returned when it applied the physical consequence of this attempt. Required before Sales records the result: Inventory owns what happened to the goods, and a sale that recorded a dispense Inventory had not yet consumed would report stock it still believes is on the shelf. Opaque here and never interpreted.
When the executor was asked. Immutable, and the field an operator uses to find an attempt that never reported back.
When a result was recorded, null while the attempt is still outstanding. The gap between this and started_at is what says a machine stopped answering.
